title: Psalm 111: Great Are the Works of the LORD
summary: In a short alphabetic hymn, the psalmist gives thanks among the upright for God's works: his wonders, his provision, his covenant faithfulness, the land he gave, and the redemption he sent. The psalm ends with the famous saying that the fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom.

from.where: The Study Bible's notes on Psalm 111

line: A short alphabetic hymn of thanks for God's works, his provision and his covenant, ending with the saying that the fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom.
guide: Ponder slowly what God has done, in the Bible's story and in your own. Ask whether you have begun where wisdom begins: not with cleverness, a degree or experience, but with the fear of the LORD.

stanzas.title: Thanks in the assembly of the upright
Food, covenant, and the gift of the land
The fear of the LORD, the beginning of wisdom

verses.t: Hallelujah! I will give thanks to the LORD with all my heart in the council of the upright and in the assembly.
Great are the works of the LORD; they are pondered by all who delight in them.
Splendid and majestic is His work; His righteousness endures forever.
He has caused His wonders to be remembered; the LORD is gracious and compassionate.
He provides food for those who fear Him; He remembers His covenant forever.
He has shown His people the power of His works by giving them the inheritance of the nations.
The works of His hands are truth and justice; all His precepts are trustworthy.
They are upheld forever and ever, enacted in truth and uprightness.
He has sent redemption to His people; He has ordained His covenant forever; holy and awesome is His name.
The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom; all who follow His precepts gain rich understanding. His praise endures forever!
